Hi Julie / Security team — thanks for the clear list. Answers below and attached artifacts. Happy to hop on a short call if you prefer a walkthrough.

1) SOC 2: The attached summary is for the most recent SOC 2 Type II (audit period 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31). Auditor: RedBridge LLP. We can provide a redacted full report under NDA — let me know and I’ll start that process.

2) EU region availability: Yes — Redwood supports EU region pinning for customer data. Production customer data, logs that contain customer PII, and KV caches can be confined to EU regions (Frankfurt or Dublin) with our Private and Dedicated modes. Hosted (shared) has configurable routing but you should plan for Dedicated or Private for strict EU-only guarantees. We do not replicate pinned EU datasets to the US for processing unless explicit cross-region failover is enabled by the customer.

3) Cross-border transfer: We support GDPR-compliant transfer mechanisms. Our standard approach is Data Processing Agreement + Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs). For customers requiring additional contractual language we can negotiate terms. If you require local data residency with no transfers, Dedicated/Private deployment is the recommended path.

4) OFAC/ITAR: Redwood does not actively screen content for ITAR classification by default. We do have controls for OFAC screening at account provisioning and block accounts/requests based on sanctions lists when required by contract. If you have specific export-control workflows, Jordan / Dev can scope technical controls (logging, rate-limiting, SRB) and any contractual protections.

Attachments: redwood_soc2_type2_summary.pdf, redwood_vendor_security_questionnaire_v1.pdf (filled copy).
